questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- Academic opportunities, with relevant english speaking courses for my degree
- International Community and ability to travel around, whilst on Exchange

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was fairly easy, I had already checked my e-mail a lot and created a profile for my new University.
They were very good at sending information about arrival and study start. It was somewhat more difficult to find information about the introduction activities

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Guided tour across campus, a brief introduction to the different platforms we would be using and a tour around the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult, start very early with searching and be aware of deadlines for signing up for housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will see a lot more of the city and meet different people, but it might be more difficult to find a place

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had a deadline two weeks before arrival, where we had to submit our requests for courses. It was however first come first serve, so all research about courses and scheduling should be done before hand. It was somewhat okay to find the information, but scheduling made it difficult to choose courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinator would answer all questions and try to help with scheduling conflicts,  but most of it is ones own responsibility

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat succesful, I got some classes I really wanted. Others were a last minute solution to fill up the required credits.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do a lot of research before hand, and have priorities ready. Be sure to check the timetable, as most courses have attendance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses had a lot of assignment, but the level was similar to that of UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller courses and a lot more groupwork and group discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- International and Global communication
- ICT's and emerging markets
- Digital Marketing
- Digital media and Health
- Media Industries: Trends and Strategies
- Feeling Orange

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International and global communication, was a really good course. The professor was very passionate about the subject, and it made a lot of sense to learn in a setting of mostly international students, as it gave a much broader perspective.
Feeling orange is a required course for all exchange students, about dutch culture. It was nice to have classes with other exchange students we had made during the exchange, and great to know more about the historical context of the culture we are in.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Flight tickets to and from places

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I got a very cheap bike subscription. Going out to eat and rent was pretty expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a big sports facility, open for everyone with teams, classes and fitness. There were also a lot of different social activities such as parties and events for all students at the university. Most of which you did not have to be a member of the committee arranging the activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The parties are a great way to meet and see other students. The campus sports centre is also a good way to spend time with other students and exercise whilst on exchange.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit all the other cities nearby, the train system is really good, so you can get really far without spending too much money. Also go exploring in the city, and get a museumspass in the beginning. It gives a lot of discounts throughout the Netherlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very similar to that of Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open-minded and ready to get to know a lot of other people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There weren't really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fried food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try a lot of different cuisines in the city it is very multi-cultural
2. The campus is a great place to study and meet people even if you don't have a lot of classes
3. Join as many intro days activities as possible, it really pays off

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to spend a lot of money, so that you don't miss out on experiences.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many nice people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being very active and therefore also very tired.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
